verdicts.reason: Both cut the dark header into an empty block at the top right, which leaves the white SOLSTICE wordmark on cream where it can't be read, so the brand breaks in both. A: the headline is big and fills the banner well. But the bottom row is jammed against the bottom edge: body copy, CTA, an oversized 'Ships late June' that competes with the CTA, and legal text too small to read. The orange divider is stranded under the logo. B is a shrunk, centred copy of the portrait original: the headline is small, the body, CTA label and legal text are tiny, the divider floats off to the right at random, and there is a lot of dead space on both sides.
